result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md: the notification batch that closes the published->cancelled cancellation flow REQ-016 deliberately deferred, now that REQ-025's send-once ledger and REQ-026's batch-loop precedent both exist.

TRIGGER MECHANISM DECIDED (Sec1): synchronous, one-time batch send from handlers/event.ts's makeEventCancelHandler, called right after cancelEvent's (REQ-016) transaction returns/commits -- NOT a scheduled/polling job. Reasoning: cancellation is a one-time organizer command, not a time-threshold condition, so scheduler/runner.ts's ScheduledJobDefinition machinery (built for REQ-026's T-24h/T-3h windows) does not fit. cancelEvent's own header comment states its explicit scope boundary ('no read of the registrations table, no notification composition/send of any kind. REQ-027's scope') -- this design does not reopen that transaction or add a third write inside it; domain/event.ts is deliberately framework-free (no grammy import) and has no way to reach a NotificationSender. The design combines two existing precedents: handlers/withdraw.ts's makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler (call the notification function synchronously right after the domain write's transaction returns, before the handler's own reply -- used there for REQ-023's single promoted registrant) and scheduler/reminderJobs.ts's makeReminder24hJob/makeReminder3hJob (select the eligible set once, then loop sendLedgeredNotification over it sequentially, no ScheduledJobDefinition wrapper needed since this runs exactly once).

SCHEMA CHANGE -- NO, confirmed by direct inspection (per this role's mandatory pre-check, stated in the design's own 'Schema change: NO' section): notification_ledger's uniqueIndex('uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind').on(registrationId, kind) already exists (schema.ts lines 361-364) -- the exact constraint AC2's idempotency rests on, unchanged by this requirement. NotificationKind (domain/notification.ts line 15-21) ALREADY CONTAINS 'event_cancelled' as a union member -- REQ-025 anticipated this requirement's kind by name when it was written, so no TypeScript union change either. registrations.admission already has a 'withdrawn' state; events.status already has 'cancelled' (REQ-016). DATA-DESIGNER does not run this cycle.

NEW READ (Sec2): selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent(db, eventId): Promise<NonWithdrawnRegistrant[]> in domain/registration.ts -- a plain SELECT of registrations.id/userId filtered on eventId and admission <> 'withdrawn', with NO time predicate and therefore no evaluationTime parameter (explicit, reasoned deviation from decisions/0006's evaluation-time-as-parameter discipline, which applies only to functions that compare against the current instant -- this one does not, since a cancellation notice is due regardless of how far away the event was).

NEW COMPOSE + ORCHESTRATION (Sec3): both placed in handlers/event.ts (not domain/, not scheduler/), mirroring exactly where withdraw.ts places sendPromotionNotification. composeCancellationMessage(db, registrationId, eventTitle, lang) re-fetches the registration's CURRENT admission via the already-existing getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent (REQ-026) at send time -- same freshness recheck composeReminder24h/composeReminder3h already perform, for the identical reason (sendLedgeredNotification calls composeMessage only after its ledger INSERT has committed, REQ-025 Sec3.1 step 5) -- and returns {kind:'skip'} if the registration is gone or now withdrawn (no events.status recheck needed: there is no un-cancel transition in the state machine, so the event cannot un-cancel between selection and send within one invocation). notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants(db, sender, eventId, eventTitle): Promise<void> selects the fixed batch list ONCE, then loops sendLedgeredNotification({..., kind:'event_cancelled', classification:'transactional', ...}) over it sequentially (same for...of shape as the reminder jobs, no Promise.all fan-out), never inspecting individual SendOutcomes -- same 'fire the batch, don't act on outcomes' contract sendPromotionNotification already establishes.

MESSAGE CONTENT (Sec4): one new catalog key, event.cancelledNotificationHeader ('This event has been cancelled:' placeholder, same prefix-then-title shape as the existing cancelSuccessPrefix). The onward path reuses the ALREADY-EXISTING event.deepLinkSeeUpcoming string ('See what's coming up with /events') verbatim -- no new onward-path string invented, satisfying the requirement's explicit instruction to reuse REQ-017's /events messaging/pattern literally. Composed text is 3 lines: header, eventTitle, deepLinkSeeUpcoming. No buttons.

HANDLER WIRING (Sec5): makeEventCancelHandler gains a sender: NotificationSender parameter (mirrors makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler(db, sender) exactly); calls notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants right after cancelEvent returns, before the handler's own ctx.reply to the organizer (same ordering withdraw.ts already uses for its post-commit promotion notification). index.ts's bot.command('event_cancel', makeEventCancelHandler(db)) becomes ...makeEventCancelHandler(db, notificationSender) -- reusing the single process-wide notificationSender index.ts already constructs, no new sender instance.

AC2 IDEMPOTENCY ARGUMENT (Sec6), stated fully in the design: structurally identical to REQ-025/REQ-026's own guarantee, extended from one registrant to a batch. sendLedgeredNotification's step 4 is the ONLY place a ledger row is ever written, as a single atomic INSERT; a repeat INSERT for the same (registrationId, 'event_cancelled') pair hits the unique index (Postgres 23505) and is classified as skipped-already-sent -- no send. notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants keeps NO in-memory state of its own (no local 'already sent' set, no counter) -- the exact negative case security-invariants.md S9 names as unacceptable ('idempotency enforced by an in-memory set that a restart clears') is structurally absent here, since the guarantee lives entirely in the DB unique constraint. Re-running the whole batch, or the handler being invoked again by any means, reduces every one of its N calls to sendLedgeredNotification's duplicate-key branch, which sends nothing -- true whether the repeat is a literal double /event_cancel (actually unreachable through the command surface, refused earlier by the existing event.status !== 'published' guard) or a process restart mid-batch (the AC's actual scenario).

All 5 ACs mapped to concrete design elements in Sec7's table. AC4 (registrations rows/admission unchanged) is defended structurally, not by a new check: none of the three new functions issue any UPDATE/DELETE against registrations, and cancelEvent itself (unchanged) only ever touches events.status and audit_log. 3 open questions stated explicitly in Sec8: the accepted send-failure-after-ledger-commit risk (restates REQ-025 Sec3.2/REQ-026's already-accepted risk, not re-solved here), a narrow withdraw-races-with-send interleaving window the at-send-time recheck does not fully close (no AC exercises it, named as residual risk of the same shape REQ-026 Sec9 already accepts), and a considered-but-not-found gap around concurrent re-registration against a cancelling event (blocked structurally by registerForEvent's existing published-only guard).
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b) -- DATA-DESIGNER does not run this cycle, no stored-data change (notification_ledger's unique index and NotificationKind's 'event_cancelled' member both already exist from REQ-025; registrations.admission's 'withdrawn' state and events.status's 'cancelled' state both already exist from REQ-011/REQ-016).
